units.title: Start Here — Processes, Threads & Why They Exist

lessons.name: What is a Process?
lessons.desc: A process is a running program. When you open Chrome, the OS creates a process for it — gives it its own memory space, CPU time, and resources. Each process is isolated; one crashing process cannot corrupt another.
lessons.q: What is a process? What resources does the OS give to each process?
lessons.qsub: Why are processes isolated from each other? What would happen if they shared memory by default?
terms: Running program ka instance — apna address space, file descriptors, PID.
Har process ko OS virtual memory deta hai; dusre process ki memory dikhti nahi.
Process Control Block — OS ka record: PID, state, registers, memory maps.
lessons.what:
Definition: Process = disk par pada program jab OS use memory mein load karke chalata hai. OS use code, heap, stack, open files aur ek PID deta hai.

Isolation hardware (MMU) enforce karta hai — ek process dusre ki memory seedhe padh/likh nahi sakta. Baat karni ho to IPC (pipes, sockets, shared memory) chahiye.
lessons.analogy: Process ek alag flat jaisa hai: apni rasoi, apna bijli meter, apna darwaza. Padosi ke flat mein aag lage to tumhara flat safe.
lessons.why: Isolation se ek buggy program poore system ko nahi girata. Browser har tab alag process mein isiliye chalata hai — tab crash ho to baaki tabs bachte hain.
where: Chrome har tab/extension ko alag process deta hai.
nginx/PM2 multiple worker processes chalate hain.
pros: Strong isolation — crash ya memory corruption contain rehta hai
cons: Data share karna IPC ke through — slow aur complex
gotchas: Process create karna thread se kaafi heavy hai
Zombie process: child exit ho gaya par parent ne wait() nahi kiya
Do processes ka PID same nahi hota par fork ke baad memory copy-on-write hoti hai

lessons.name: What is a Thread?
lessons.desc: A thread is a single sequence of execution inside a process. One process can have many threads — they share the same memory (heap, code, files) but each has its own stack and CPU registers. Threads are "lightweight processes" — much cheaper to create.
lessons.q: What is a thread? How is it different from a process?
lessons.qsub: If threads share memory, what is the danger? Give a simple example of two threads corrupting shared data.
terms: Process ke andar execution ka ek sequence — apna stack aur registers.
Thread ID; OS thread ko schedule karta hai.
Same process ke saare threads same heap/globals dekhte hain.
lessons.what:
Definition: Thread CPU scheduling ki sabse chhoti unit hai. Ek process mein ek ya zyada threads hote hain jo code, heap aur file descriptors share karte hain, par stack aur program counter alag rakhte hain.

Shared memory ki wajah se threads aapas mein tezi se data exchange kar sakte hain — par yahi sabse badi bug-source bhi hai.
lessons.analogy: Ek process = ek restaurant. Threads = uske waiters. Sab same rasoi (heap) aur menu share karte hain, par har waiter ka apna order-notepad (stack) hai.
lessons.why: Ek hi program mein kaam parallel ya overlap karne ka sasta tareeka: UI thread responsive rahe aur background thread file/network ka kaam kare.
where: Har request ke liye thread ya pool se thread.
pros: Process se halka — creation aur switch sasta
Memory share hone se communication fast
cons: Shared state = race conditions aur deadlocks
Ek thread ka crash poore process ko gira sakta hai
gotchas: t.run() call karne se naya thread nahi banta, normal method call hota hai
Har thread ka stack (≈1MB) memory khata hai — hazaaron threads banana costly
Thread ka output order non-deterministic hai

lessons.name: Why Do We Need Multiple Threads?
lessons.desc: Two reasons: (1) Responsiveness — while one thread waits for a disk read, another thread can keep the UI running. (2) Performance — on a multi-core CPU, threads can truly run in parallel, speeding up computation. Without threads, a web server could only handle one request at a time.
lessons.q: Why do we use multiple threads? Give a real example of a program that benefits from threading.
lessons.qsub: A web server receives 1000 simultaneous requests. How do threads help? What is a thread pool?
terms: Slow kaam background mein, UI/main flow block nahi hota.
Multi-core par ek saath zyada kaam.
Ek thread I/O par wait kare to dusra CPU use kare.
lessons.what:
Definition: Multiple threads ke do bade fayde hain: (1) responsiveness — blocking kaam alag thread mein, (2) parallelism — multi-core CPU ka poora use.

Jab ek thread disk/network par wait kar raha ho, CPU khali baithne ki jagah dusre thread ko mil jaata hai.
lessons.why: Aaj ki machines multi-core hain; single thread sirf ek core use karega. Server ko hazaaron concurrent clients bhi serve karne hote hain.
lessons.code:
# Python: I/O-bound kaam threads se overlap
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import urllib.request

urls = ['https://example.com'] * 5
def fetch(u): return len(urllib.request.urlopen(u).read())

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as ex:
    print(list(ex.map(fetch, urls)))   # 5 requests ek saath
where: Network wait ke dauraan dusre pages fetch.
gotchas: Threads CPU-bound kaam ko tabhi tez karte hain jab real cores hon (aur Python mein GIL ke bina nahi)
Zyada threads hamesha zyada speed nahi — ek limit ke baad slower
Amdahl's law: serial hissa speedup ki upper limit tay karta hai

lessons.name: Process vs Thread — Memory Model
lessons.desc: Process: own code, own heap, own stack, own file descriptors — fully isolated. Thread: shared code, shared heap, shared file descriptors — but own stack and own registers. This shared heap is the source of all concurrency bugs.
lessons.q: Draw the memory layout of a process with 3 threads. What is shared? What is private?
lessons.qsub: Creating a new process (fork) is expensive — why? Creating a thread is cheap — why?
terms: Process alag memory; thread shared memory.
Process switch mein address-space switch + TLB flush, thread mein kam.
Process ke beech communication ke liye pipes/sockets/shared mem.
lessons.what:
Definition: Process ke paas apna code, heap, stack, file descriptors hote hain (poora isolated). Thread ek process ke andar rehta hai — code, heap, globals share karta hai, sirf stack aur registers apne hote hain.

ProcessThread
MemoryAlagShared heap
CreationHeavyLight
CrashContainedPoora process
Comm.IPCDirect memory
lessons.why: Design choice: safety chahiye to process, speed aur sharing chahiye to thread. Interview mein ye trade-off sabse common question hai.
cons: Thread: races, ek bug sab giraye
gotchas: Threads ka stack alag hota hai — heap nahi
fork() ke baad child ko parent ki memory ka copy-on-write mapping milta hai
Interview trap: 'threads ko alag address space milta hai' — galat

lessons.name: How the CPU Runs Multiple Threads — Scheduling & Context Switch
lessons.desc: A CPU core can only run one thread at a time. The OS scheduler rapidly switches between threads (context switch) — saving one thread's registers and loading another's. This happens so fast (milliseconds) it feels simultaneous. Multi-core CPUs can truly run threads in parallel.
lessons.q: How does a single-core CPU appear to run multiple programs at once?
lessons.qsub: What is a context switch? What data must be saved and restored? Why does context switching have a cost?
terms: OS ka part jo tay karta hai ab kaunsa thread CPU par chalega.
Chalte thread ka state save karke dusre ka load karna.
Thread ko ek baar mein milne wala CPU time (ms).
lessons.what:
Definition: Ek core ek samay mein ek hi thread chalata hai. Scheduler time-slice khatam hone par (preemption) ya thread ke block hone par state (registers, PC) save karke dusra thread chalata hai — ise context switch kehte hain.

Switch ka kaam seedha productive nahi hota; cache bhi thanda ho jaata hai.
lessons.analogy: Ek chef (core) kai dishes sambhal raha hai — thodi der ek dish, phir note karke dusri. Dikhta hai sab saath ban rahi hain, par chef ek hi hai.
lessons.why: Isi se illusion banta hai ki hazaaron threads saath chal rahe hain. Par zyada threads = zyada switches = overhead.
lessons.code:
# Linux par context switches dekho
$ pidstat -w -p <PID> 1      # voluntary vs involuntary switches
$ vmstat 1                    # 'cs' column = system-wide context switches/sec
$ nproc                       # cores kitne hain
where: Thread pool size cores ke hisaab se.
pros: I/O wait ke time CPU waste nahi
gotchas: Voluntary switch (I/O wait) vs involuntary (time slice khatam) alag cheezein
Thread count ≫ cores CPU-bound kaam ko slow karta hai
Process switch thread switch se mahanga hai (TLB flush)

lessons.name: Concurrency vs Parallelism
lessons.desc: Concurrency: multiple tasks make progress (interleaving). Parallelism: multiple tasks run simultaneously (multi-core).
lessons.q: What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism? Give a real-world analogy.
lessons.qsub: Node.js is concurrent but not parallel. Explain what that means. How does Go achieve both?
terms: Kai tasks ek saath progress karte hain — interleaving, ek core par bhi.
Kai tasks literally ek hi time par chalte hain — multi-core.
'Concurrency is about dealing with lots of things at once; parallelism is about doing lots of things at once.'
lessons.what:
Definition: Concurrency ek structure/design property hai — program ko independent tasks mein todna. Parallelism execution property hai — un tasks ko multiple cores par ek saath chalana.

Concurrent program single core par bhi sahi chal sakta hai; parallelism ke liye hardware chahiye. Node.js event loop concurrent hai par JS code parallel nahi.
lessons.analogy: Ek cashier do line sambhale (baari-baari) = concurrency. Do cashier, har ek ek line = parallelism.
lessons.why: I/O-bound kaam ke liye concurrency kaafi hai; CPU-bound kaam ke liye parallelism chahiye. Galat tool chunna performance kharab karta hai.
pros: Concurrency: simple resource use, scalable I/O
gotchas: Concurrent ≠ parallel — interview ka favourite
Parallel hamesha concurrent hota hai, ulta nahi
Threads banana parallelism ki guarantee nahi (GIL, single core)

lessons.name: Race Condition
lessons.desc: When two threads access shared data concurrently and at least one writes — result depends on execution order.
lessons.q: What is a race condition? Write a code example that demonstrates one.
lessons.qsub: How do you detect race conditions? What tools exist (ThreadSanitizer, Helgrind)?
terms: Result thread scheduling ke order par depend kare.
count++ asal mein read, add, write — 3 steps.
Debug karte hi gayab hone wala non-deterministic bug.
lessons.what:
Definition: Jab do ya zyada threads shared data ko ek saath access karein aur kam se kam ek write kare, aur outcome timing par depend kare.

count++ atomic nahi hai: read → add → write. Do threads dono ne 5 padha, dono ne 6 likha — ek update kho gaya (lost update).
lessons.why: Race bugs production mein kabhi-kabhi aate hain, test mein nahi — paise ya inventory galat ho sakti hai (double booking, negative balance).
where: Do requests ek hi row ek saath update karein.
pros: (Bug hai — pros nahi) Samajhne se design behtar hota hai
gotchas: Check-then-act (if (!exists) create) classic race hai
Data race aur race condition alag cheezein hain — dono ho sakte hain
'Mere machine par chal raha hai' — races load par dikhte hain

lessons.name: Critical Section & Mutual Exclusion
lessons.desc: A code region accessing shared resources. Must be executed by only one thread at a time (mutual exclusion).
lessons.q: What is a critical section? What are the 4 requirements for a correct mutual exclusion solution?
lessons.qsub: What is progress and bounded waiting in the context of mutual exclusion?
terms: Code ka hissa jo shared resource chhuta hai.
Ek samay par sirf ek thread andar.
Koi thread hamesha ke liye bahar na rahe.
lessons.what:
Definition: Critical section wo code region hai jahan shared data access hota hai. Sahi solution ke teen gun: mutual exclusion, progress (koi andar nahi to doosre ko ghusne do), bounded waiting (starvation nahi).

Lock ya mutex se ise protect karte hain; section jitna chhota, utna better concurrency.
lessons.why: Chhota critical section = kam contention = zyada throughput. Bada lock sab threads ko serial bana deta hai.
lessons.code:
import threading
lock = threading.Lock()
balance = 100

def withdraw(n):
    global balance
    with lock:                 # critical section start
        if balance >= n:
            balance -= n
    # critical section end — lock auto-release
gotchas: Lock ke andar slow I/O mat karo
Exception par lock release hona chahiye — try/finally ya with
Alag locks se same data protect karna kaam nahi karta

lessons.name: Atomicity
lessons.desc: An operation that appears to happen instantaneously — no intermediate state is observable to other threads.
lessons.q: What does atomic mean? Is i++ atomic? What about a read-modify-write on a 64-bit int on a 32-bit system?
lessons.qsub: What is the happens-before relationship? How does it relate to the Java Memory Model?
terms: Operation poora hota hai ya bilkul nahi; beech ki state koi nahi dekhta.
Beech mein interrupt nahi ho sakta.
lessons.what:
Definition: Atomic operation ek instant mein hota hua dikhta hai. Hardware kuch operations (aligned read/write, CAS, fetch-add) ko atomic banata hai; baaki ke liye lock ya atomic library chahiye.

x++, x = x + 1 normally atomic nahi hain.
lessons.why: Lock ke bina simple counters aur flags safe banane ka sabse sasta tareeka atomics hain.
cons: Multi-variable invariants ke liye lock chahiye
gotchas: Do atomic ops ka combination atomic nahi hota (check-then-act)
Atomicity ≠ visibility ordering ka poora jawab
64-bit long/double kuch platforms par atomic nahi

lessons.name: Memory Visibility & CPU Caches
lessons.desc: CPUs have private caches — writes by one thread may not be visible to others without synchronization.
lessons.q: Why can a thread read stale data even without a race condition? What is the volatile keyword for?
lessons.qsub: What is a memory barrier? What is cache coherence (MESI protocol)?
terms: Har core ka private L1/L2 — writes turant dusre core ko nahi dikhte.
Ek thread ki write kab dusre thread ko dikhe.
Ordering rule jo visibility guarantee karta hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: Modern CPU aur compiler reorder/cache karte hain. Ek thread ne flag = true likha, par dusra thread purani value cache se padhta reh sakta hai — bina synchronization ke guarantee nahi.

Lock, volatile, atomics visibility ke liye memory barriers lagate hain.
lessons.why: Ye bug 'while(!done)' loop jo kabhi khatam nahi hota — jaise subtle problems ka kaaran hai.
pros: Rules samajhne par predictable concurrent code
gotchas: x86 par chalne wala code ARM par toot sakta hai
Visibility aur atomicity alag problems hain
Lock lena/chhodna bhi memory barrier hai

lessons.name: Mutex (Mutual Exclusion Lock)
lessons.desc: A lock that only one thread can hold at a time. Thread acquires lock, enters critical section, releases lock.
lessons.q: How does a mutex work? What is a spinlock and when is it better than a blocking mutex?
lessons.qsub: What is a reentrant/recursive mutex? What problem does it solve?
terms: Ek samay mein ek hi owner wala lock.
Same thread dobara lock le sake bina deadlock.
lessons.what:
Definition: Mutex critical section ko protect karta hai. Jo thread lock leta hai wahi chhodta hai (ownership). Lock mila hua ho to dusre thread block (sleep) ho jaate hain.

Reentrant mutex ek hi thread ko baar-baar lene deta hai (count rakhta hai).
lessons.why: Shared data ko sahi rakhne ka sabse basic tool — baaki primitives isi par bane hain.
pros: Sleep karta hai — CPU waste nahi
gotchas: Unlock bhoolna = poora system hang
Lock ke andar callbacks/I/O mat chalao
Non-reentrant mutex ko same thread dobara le to self-deadlock

lessons.name: Semaphore
lessons.desc: A counter-based synchronization primitive. Binary semaphore = mutex. Counting semaphore = limit concurrent access.
lessons.q: What is a semaphore? How does it differ from a mutex? Implement a bounded buffer using semaphores.
lessons.qsub: Can a thread release a semaphore it didn't acquire? How is that useful?
terms: N permits; acquire se ghatta, release se badhta.
lessons.what:
Definition: Semaphore ek counter hai. acquire() counter ghatata hai (0 ho to block), release() badhata hai. Isse N threads tak ko resource access de sakte ho.

Mutex se fark: semaphore ko koi bhi thread release kar sakta hai, isliye signaling ke liye bhi use hota hai.
lessons.analogy: Parking lot jisme 5 slots hain: gaadi aaye to slot lo, bhar gaya to bahar intezar, koi nikle to ek slot free.
lessons.why: Connection pools, rate limiting aur producer-consumer buffers mein 'max N concurrent' enforce karne ke liye.
cons: Ownership nahi — galat release se bug
gotchas: release() bhool gaye to permits leak
Semaphore(1) aur mutex ek cheez nahi
Zyada release se count limit se upar ja sakta hai

lessons.name: Monitor & Condition Variables
lessons.desc: A monitor combines a mutex + condition variables. A thread can wait() until a condition is true, then be signal()ed.
lessons.q: What is a monitor? How do condition variables work? Why must you always check conditions in a while loop?
lessons.qsub: What is a spurious wakeup? Why can they happen and how do you handle them?
terms: Lock chhod ke sleep; signal par wapas lock lekar jaagta hai.
Bina signal ke bhi jaag sakta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Monitor mein lock ke andar thread kisi condition ka wait kar sakta hai (wait), aur dusra thread condition badal kar notify/signal kar deta hai. wait atomic roop se lock release karke sleep karta hai.
lessons.why: Busy-waiting CPU jalati hai; condition variable thread ko sula kar efficient coordination deta hai (queue empty/full jaise cases).
cons: Missed signal / lost wakeup ka risk
gotchas: Hamesha while mein condition check karo (spurious wakeup)
wait/notify sirf lock hold karke
notify() sirf ek thread jagata hai — galat thread jaag sakta hai

lessons.name: Read-Write Lock
lessons.desc: Multiple readers can hold simultaneously. Only one writer — exclusive. Perfect for read-heavy workloads.
lessons.q: When would you use a Read-Write Lock over a plain mutex? What are its trade-offs?
lessons.qsub: What is writer starvation? How do some implementations prevent it?
terms: Readers lagatar aate rahein to writer ruka rahe.
lessons.what: Definition: ReadWriteLock multiple readers ya ek writer allow karta hai. Read-heavy workload (95% reads) mein mutex se behtar throughput deta hai.
lessons.why: Reads ko serialize karna waste hai jab wo data badalte hi nahi.
gotchas: Read lock ko write lock mein upgrade karna aksar deadlock karta hai
Write-heavy workload mein mutex se slow
Fair vs non-fair policy samajh kar chuno

lessons.name: Barrier & Latch
lessons.desc: Barrier: all threads must reach it before any proceeds. Latch: countdown to zero then releases all waiters.
lessons.q: What is a CyclicBarrier? What is a CountDownLatch? When would you use each?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between a CountDownLatch and a Semaphore?
terms: N threads wait karte hain jab tak sab pahunch na jayein.
Count 0 hone par ek baar sab release; reuse nahi.
Parallel algorithm ke steps jo sync maangte hain.
lessons.what: Definition: CyclicBarrier reusable hai — har phase ke baad sab ek saath aage badhte hain. CountDownLatch ek-baar: main thread tab tak wait karta hai jab tak workers countDown() na kar dein.
lessons.why: Parallel simulations/matrix steps mein agle phase ko pichle phase ka poora data chahiye hota hai.
where: Sab services ready hone ka wait.
cons: Ek thread atak jaye to sab atak jaate hain
gotchas: Latch dobara use nahi hota
Barrier mein ek thread fail ho to BrokenBarrierException
Worker exception par countDown finally mein karo

lessons.name: Four Conditions for Deadlock
lessons.desc: Coffman conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait. All 4 must hold.
lessons.q: What are the four necessary conditions for deadlock? To prevent deadlock, which one would you eliminate?
lessons.qsub: Draw a resource allocation graph and show how it demonstrates a deadlock.
lessons.what:
Definition: Deadlock tab hota hai jab Coffman ki chaaron conditions ek saath hon. Inme se ek bhi tod do to deadlock nahi ho sakta.

Classic: Thread 1 ne lock A liya, B maanga; Thread 2 ne B liya, A maanga.
lessons.analogy: Chaurahe par chaaron taraf se gaadiyan fans gayi — koi peeche nahi hat sakta, sab agle ka wait kar rahe hain.
lessons.why: Chaaron yaad rakhne se prevention strategy turant samajh aati hai: har condition ek tarah ka fix suggest karti hai.
where: Dono taraf se lock lene wale.
cons: Runtime par rare aur reproduce karna mushkil
gotchas: Chaaron conditions hone chahiye — ek todo, solve
Database deadlock detection ke baad ek transaction abort karta hai
Thread dump (jstack) se cycle dikhta hai

lessons.name: Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance
lessons.desc: Prevention: eliminate one Coffman condition. Avoidance: Banker's algorithm. Detection: find cycles in RAG.
lessons.q: Compare deadlock prevention, avoidance (Banker's algorithm), and detection. What does each cost?
lessons.qsub: Why is the Banker's algorithm rarely used in practice? What do real OSes do instead?
terms: Banker's algorithm — safe state mein hi allocate.
Wait-for graph mein cycle dhoondho, phir recover.
lessons.what: Definition: Prevention: lock ordering (circular wait), sab locks ek saath lena (hold & wait), tryLock+timeout (no preemption). Avoidance system-state dekh kar decide karta hai. Detection+recovery: cycle mile to ek victim abort.
lessons.why: Production mein practical tareeka lock ordering + timeouts + chhote critical sections hai.
cons: tryLock se livelock ho sakta hai
gotchas: Timeout lagana cause nahi chhupata — log karo
Retry mein random backoff
Banker's algorithm real systems mein shaayad hi use hota hai

lessons.name: Livelock & Starvation
lessons.desc: Livelock: threads keep responding to each other but make no progress. Starvation: a thread never gets CPU time.
lessons.q: What is the difference between deadlock, livelock, and starvation? Give a real-world analogy for each.
lessons.qsub: How do you avoid livelock when implementing retry logic? What is exponential backoff?
terms: Threads active hain par progress zero.
Ek thread ko resource kabhi nahi milta.
lessons.what: Definition: Deadlock mein threads block hote hain; livelock mein wo chalte rehte hain par kuch kaam nahi hota. Starvation mein scheduler/lock policy ki wajah se ek thread hamesha peeche reh jaata hai.
lessons.analogy: Corridor mein do log ek-dusre ko raasta dene ke chakkar mein dono ek hi taraf hat rahe hain — dono hil rahe hain, par aage koi nahi badh raha.
lessons.why: Retry loops aur unfair locks mein ye dikhte hain; CPU 100% par aur throughput zero.
cons: Diagnose mushkil — CPU busy dikhta hai
gotchas: Starvation fix: fair locks, aging
Fixed retry delay dono ko sync rakhta hai
Priority inversion alag problem hai

lessons.name: Lock Ordering & Practical Deadlock Prevention
lessons.desc: Acquire locks in a consistent global order across all threads — the most practical deadlock prevention technique.
lessons.q: How does consistent lock ordering prevent deadlock? What is tryLock with timeout?
lessons.qsub: Show a bank transfer example where two threads deadlock without lock ordering, and how to fix it.
terms: Saare locks ka ek fixed rank.
lessons.what: Definition: Agar har thread locks ek hi order mein le (jaise account id ke ascending order mein), to circular wait possible nahi, isliye deadlock nahi.
lessons.why: Bank transfer(A→B) aur transfer(B→A) ek saath chalein to deadlock hota hai — ordering se fix.
cons: Dynamic locks mein order pata karna mushkil
gotchas: Equal id/hash par tie-breaker lock
Callbacks ke andar naye locks hidden order tod dete hain
Order document karo

lessons.name: Thread Pools
lessons.desc: Pre-created pool of threads that pick up tasks from a queue. Avoids thread creation overhead, controls resource usage.
lessons.q: Why use a thread pool instead of creating a new thread per task? How do you size a thread pool?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between a fixed thread pool and a cached thread pool? What is a work-stealing pool?
terms: Pehle se bane, reuse hote hain.
Queue bhar jaye to kya karna hai.
lessons.what:
Definition: Thread pool fixed/bounded threads rakhta hai jo queue se tasks uthate hain. Thread creation cost bachta hai aur concurrency limit hoti hai.

Sizing: CPU-bound ≈ cores; I/O-bound ≈ cores × (1 + wait/compute).
lessons.why: Unbounded thread-per-request server load par memory khatam karke crash ho jaata hai.
gotchas: Pool ke andar pool ka wait karne wale tasks deadlock karte hain
Unbounded queue memory leak jaisa
shutdown() bhoolne par JVM exit nahi hota

lessons.name: Compare-And-Swap (CAS) & Atomic Operations
lessons.desc: Hardware-supported instruction: atomically compare memory location to expected value and swap if equal. No lock needed.
lessons.q: How does CAS work? Implement an atomic counter using CAS. What is the ABA problem?
lessons.qsub: What is an AtomicReference? How does it differ from a volatile reference?
terms: CAS fail ho to phir se padho aur try karo.
Value A→B→A ho gayi, CAS ko pata nahi.
lessons.what: Definition: CAS CPU instruction hai: memory mein value expected ke barabar ho to nayi value likho, warna fail. Is par lock-free counters/stacks bante hain.
lessons.why: Lock ke bina atomic update — contention kam hoti hai aur deadlock nahi.
gotchas: ABA fix: version stamp (AtomicStampedReference)
Heavy contention mein LongAdder behtar
CAS ek variable par hi atomic hai

lessons.name: Lock-Free & Wait-Free Algorithms
lessons.desc: Lock-free: system-wide progress guaranteed (at least one thread progresses). Wait-free: every thread progresses.
lessons.q: What is a lock-free data structure? Why is it hard to implement? When would you use one?
lessons.qsub: Is lock-free always faster than locked? What overhead does CAS have?
terms: Kam se kam ek thread hamesha aage badhta hai.
Har thread bounded steps mein khatam.
lessons.what: Definition: Lock-free algorithms mutex ki jagah CAS use karte hain, isliye ek thread ka stall/suspension baakiyon ko block nahi karta. Wait-free sabse strong guarantee hai par likhna bahut mushkil.
lessons.why: Low-latency systems (trading, kernels) mein lock ka blocking aur priority inversion bardasht nahi hota.
gotchas: Lock-free ≠ hamesha tez
Pehle proven library use karo, khud mat likho
Starvation individual thread ki ho sakti hai

lessons.name: Futures, Promises & Async/Await
lessons.desc: A Future represents a value not yet computed. Promise resolves it later. Async/await is syntactic sugar over Futures.
lessons.q: What is the difference between a Future and a Promise? How does CompletableFuture in Java work?
lessons.qsub: What is structured concurrency? How does it improve on raw threads and futures?
terms: Abhi na mili value ka placeholder.
Value set karne wala writable side.
lessons.what: Definition: Future ek pending result hai jo baad mein resolve ya reject hota hai. async/await compiler/runtime state machine banata hai jo await par thread chhod deta hai (block nahi karta).
lessons.why: Callback hell ke bina asynchronous kaam compose karna (chain, all, race) aur errors ek jagah handle karna.
cons: Sequential await galti se serial ho jaata hai
gotchas: await loop mein serial hota hai — Promise.all use karo
Future.get() blocking hai
Unhandled rejection process crash kar sakta hai

lessons.name: Actor Model
lessons.desc: Concurrency without shared state — actors communicate via message passing only. Used in Erlang, Akka, Go channels.
lessons.q: Explain the Actor model. How does it avoid race conditions without locks?
lessons.qsub: How do Go goroutines and channels implement the Actor model? What is "Share memory by communicating"?
terms: Private state + mailbox; ek time par ek message.
Parent actor child ke fail par restart tay karta hai (Erlang).
lessons.what:
Definition: Actor model mein har actor apni state ka akela maalik hai; doosre actor sirf message bhej sakte hain. Mailbox ke messages ek-ek karke process hote hain, isliye locks ki zaroorat nahi.

Go ka mantra: 'share memory by communicating'.
lessons.why: Shared mutable state hata do to races khatam. Distributed systems par bhi naturally scale hota hai.
gotchas: Mailbox unbounded ho to OOM
Actor ke andar blocking call poora actor rokta hai
Request-reply pattern deadlock kar sakta hai

lessons.name: Memory Ordering — sequential consistency, acquire-release, relaxed
lessons.desc: Memory ordering defines the order in which memory operations become visible to other threads. Sequential consistency: all threads see the same order. Acquire-release: release on write, acquire on read (synchronizes). Relaxed: no ordering guarantees (fastest). x86 is mostly TSO (Total Store Order). ARM/POWER are weakly ordered.
lessons.q: What is the difference between sequential consistency and relaxed memory ordering?
lessons.qsub: When would you use acquire-release vs relaxed ordering? How does the Java Memory Model define volatile?
terms: Saare threads ek hi global order dekhte hain.
Release se pehle ki writes acquire karne wale ko dikhengi.
lessons.what: Definition: CPU/compiler instructions reorder karte hain. Memory model tay karta hai kaun si orderings guaranteed hain. SC sabse safe aur slow; acquire-release publish pattern ke liye kaafi; relaxed counters ke liye.
lessons.why: Lock-free code sahi likhne ke liye zaroori — galat ordering par bug sirf kisi architecture par dikhta hai.
gotchas: Default seq_cst rakho jab tak profile na kahe
Relaxed se data publish nahi hota
x86 strong hai, ARM weak — testing dono par

lessons.name: volatile keyword — Java, C++, JavaScript differences
lessons.desc: Java volatile: visibility guarantee (no caching) + happens-before ordering. C++ volatile: prevents compiler optimization (NOT thread-safe, use std::atomic). JavaScript: no volatile (single-threaded). Common misconception: volatile does NOT provide atomicity in Java.
lessons.q: What does volatile guarantee in Java? Why is it NOT sufficient for thread safety?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between volatile in Java and C++? Why doesn't JavaScript need volatile?
terms: volatile nahi hota; Atomics use karo.
lessons.what: Definition: Java mein volatile variable ki write turant sab threads ko dikhti hai aur reordering rokti hai. Par volatile int x; x++ atomic nahi. C++ mein volatile threading ke liye nahi hai (std::atomic use karo).
lessons.why: Flags (stop/ready) ke liye perfect; counters ke liye galat tool.
gotchas: volatile count++ race hai
C++ volatile ≠ Java volatile
Double-checked singleton mein volatile zaroori

lessons.name: Thread Interruption — cooperative cancellation, InterruptedException, flags
lessons.desc: Thread interruption is cooperative: interrupt sets a flag, the thread must check and respond. Java: Thread.interrupt() + InterruptedException. Python: threading.Event. Go: context.Context with cancel. Never ignore InterruptedException — either rethrow or restore interrupt flag.
lessons.q: How does cooperative thread cancellation work? Why is it preferred over forceful termination?
lessons.qsub: What happens if you catch InterruptedException without rethrowing? How do you implement cancellation in Go with context?
terms: Thread ko khud check karke ruk-na hota hai.
Blocking call interrupt par throw karta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Thread ko zabardasti maarna unsafe hai (locks leak). Isliye interrupt sirf flag set karta hai; thread blocking calls par ya isInterrupted() check karke cleanly exit karta hai.
lessons.why: Graceful shutdown aur timeouts ke liye cancellation zaroori hai bina resources leak kiye.
cons: Code cooperate na kare to cancel nahi hota
gotchas: InterruptedException swallow mat karo — flag restore karo
Thread.stop deprecated/unsafe
CPU loop mein check na ho to interrupt kaam nahi karega

lessons.name: Green Threads vs OS Threads — fibers, coroutines, M:N scheduling
lessons.desc: Green threads (goroutines, Kotlin coroutines, Python asyncio tasks) are multiplexed onto OS threads by a runtime. M:N model: M green threads on N OS threads. Lightweight (~2KB stack for goroutines vs ~1MB for OS threads). Scheduled by runtime, not OS. Blocked green thread yields OS thread.
lessons.q: What is the difference between green threads and OS threads? How does M:N scheduling work?
lessons.qsub: How do goroutines differ from Java threads? What is the stack growth strategy for goroutines?
terms: M green threads N OS threads par.
lessons.what: Definition: Green threads runtime ke scheduler se chalte hain, OS ke nahi. Blocking I/O par runtime thread ko park karke OS thread dusre green thread ko de deta hai. Isliye lakhon concurrent tasks possible.
lessons.why: Thread-per-request ka simple code style, par async jaisi scalability.
cons: CPU-bound kaam scheduler ko starve kar sakta hai
Native blocking calls pin kar dete hain
gotchas: Goroutine leak — exit path zaroori
Virtual threads pooling ke liye nahi hain
CPU-bound par parallelism cores se hi limited

lessons.name: Event Loop Deep Dive
lessons.desc: JS is single-threaded but non-blocking via event loop: call stack + task queue + microtask queue + libuv.
lessons.q: Explain the JS event loop in detail. What is the difference between microtasks and macrotasks?
lessons.qsub: In what order do these run: setTimeout(0), Promise.resolve(), queueMicrotask(), setImmediate()?
lessons.what: Definition: Loop: stack khali ho → saari microtasks drain → ek macrotask → repeat. Node mein libuv phases hain (timers, poll, check) aur process.nextTick microtasks se bhi pehle.
lessons.why: Ordering aur blocking samajhna — ek heavy sync function poore server ko freeze kar deta hai.
cons: CPU-bound kaam loop block karta hai
gotchas: Microtask loop (recursive then) macrotasks ko starve karta hai
setTimeout(0) turant nahi chalta
JSON.parse bade payload par loop block

lessons.name: Worker Threads in Node.js
lessons.desc: Node.js Worker Threads enable true parallelism for CPU-bound work. Each worker has its own V8 and event loop.
lessons.q: When would you use Worker Threads in Node.js? How do you communicate between them?
lessons.qsub: What is SharedArrayBuffer? How does it enable shared memory between workers? What synchronization do you need?
lessons.what: Definition: worker_threads CPU-heavy kaam main loop se hata deta hai. Workers memory share nahi karte (default) — messages copy hote hain; SharedArrayBuffer se share kar sakte ho.
lessons.why: Image resize, hashing, parsing jaise kaam main thread par API ko slow nahi karte.
gotchas: I/O ke liye worker ki zaroorat nahi
Har request par naya worker banana mahanga — pool use karo
Functions postMessage nahi ho sakte

lessons.name: Promise Internals & Error Handling
lessons.desc: Promises implement the microtask queue. Unhandled promise rejections can crash Node.js in newer versions.
lessons.q: How do Promises work internally? What is Promise chaining vs async/await? What are the error propagation rules?
lessons.qsub: What is Promise.all vs Promise.allSettled vs Promise.race vs Promise.any? When do you use each?
terms: Har then naya promise return karta hai.
lessons.what: Definition: Promise ke callbacks microtask queue mein chalte hain. then ka return value agle promise ko resolve karta hai; throw rejection mein badal jaata hai.
lessons.why: Error propagation aur ordering ke bugs samajhne ke liye.
gotchas: then mein return bhoolna chain tod deta hai
async function ke bina await ka error catch nahi hota
Promise.all ek fail par fast-reject karta hai — allSettled alag

lessons.name: Node.js Cluster & Load Balancing
lessons.desc: Node Cluster forks multiple worker processes (one per CPU core) sharing the same port — achieves parallelism.
lessons.q: How does Node.js Cluster module work? How does the master process distribute connections to workers?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between using Cluster and running multiple Node.js instances behind a load balancer?
terms: Master fork karta hai, workers port share karte hain.
lessons.what: Definition: cluster module har CPU core par ek Node process chalata hai, sab ek hi port par. Memory share nahi hoti, isliye in-memory session/cache workers ke beech consistent nahi.
lessons.why: Single-threaded Node ek core hi use karta hai; cluster se throughput multi-core par badhta hai aur ek worker crash par baaki chalte rehte hain.
where: Aksar ek process per container + orchestrator.
gotchas: WebSocket sticky sessions chahiye
In-memory cache har worker ka alag
K8s mein cluster ki jagah pod replicas

lessons.name: Producer-Consumer Problem
lessons.desc: Producers add items to a bounded buffer; consumers remove items. Synchronize to avoid overflow and underflow.
lessons.q: Implement the Producer-Consumer problem using semaphores. Then solve it with a BlockingQueue.
lessons.qsub: How does a message queue system like Kafka implement the producer-consumer pattern at scale?
terms: Fixed size queue — backpressure deta hai.
Consumer empty par, producer full par wait.
lessons.what: Definition: Producers queue mein items daalte hain, consumers nikalte hain. Bounded buffer producers ko slow karta hai jab consumers peeche hon (backpressure).
lessons.why: Decoupling aur load smoothing — message queues, logging pipelines, worker pools sab isi par bane hain.
gotchas: Unbounded queue memory fill karti hai
Shutdown ke liye poison pill ya close signal
Ek consumer slow ho to queue bhar jaati hai

lessons.name: Readers-Writers Problem
lessons.desc: Multiple readers can read simultaneously. Writers need exclusive access. Variants: reader-first vs writer-first.
lessons.q: Solve the Readers-Writers problem. Which variant prevents starvation and how?
lessons.qsub: How does a database implement this pattern for MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control)?
terms: Readers ko priority — writer starve ho sakta hai.
Writer wait mein ho to naye readers rokte hain.
lessons.what: Definition: Shared data par kai readers ek saath, writer exclusive. Variants fairness tay karte hain. Solution: ReadWriteLock ya semaphores + reader count.
lessons.why: Read-heavy caches/configs mein performance aur fairness ka balance.
gotchas: Reader-preference mein writer bhookha reh sakta hai
Reader count update bhi mutex se
Production mein ready ReadWriteLock use karo

lessons.name: Dining Philosophers Problem
lessons.desc: N philosophers alternate eating/thinking, sharing N forks. Demonstrates deadlock and starvation challenges.
lessons.q: Explain the Dining Philosophers problem. Give two different solutions to avoid deadlock.
lessons.qsub: What does this problem teach about real-world lock acquisition patterns?
terms: Sab ne left fork utha li → deadlock.
Forks ko number do, chhota pehle.
lessons.what: Definition: N philosophers ko khane ke liye do forks chahiye. Sab ek saath left fork uthayein to deadlock. Fixes: fork ordering, max N−1 philosophers table par (semaphore), ya odd/even alag order.
lessons.why: Deadlock/starvation ka standard model; interview mein lock ordering explain karne ka example.
gotchas: Semaphore(N-1) bhi kaam karta hai
Ordering fix starvation nahi hataata
Real fix = fewer locks

lessons.name: Thread-Safe Singleton
lessons.desc: Creating a singleton in a multi-threaded environment — naive lazy initialization is not thread-safe.
lessons.q: What is wrong with double-checked locking for Singleton? How do you implement it correctly?
lessons.qsub: What is the Initialization-on-Demand Holder idiom? Why is it the cleanest approach?
terms: Pehle bina lock check, phir lock mein.
lessons.what: Definition: Naive if (inst==null) inst=new X() do threads mein do instances bana sakta hai. Safe options: eager static, holder class, enum, ya volatile + double-checked locking.
lessons.why: Reordering ki wajah se half-constructed object dikh sakta hai — volatile bina DCL toota hua hai.
gotchas: volatile ke bina DCL broken
Class loader alag ho to multiple instances
DI container behtar option

lessons.name: Design a Thread-Safe Rate Limiter
lessons.desc: Token bucket or leaky bucket algorithm implemented with atomic operations or locks for concurrent requests.
lessons.q: Design a thread-safe rate limiter that allows 100 req/sec. Implement it in code.
lessons.qsub: How would you make it distributed across multiple servers? What data store would you use?
terms: Tokens refill hote hain, burst allow.
lessons.what: Definition: Token bucket: capacity C, refill rate r. Har request ek token leti hai. Thread-safe banane ke liye lock ya CAS par (tokens, lastRefill) ko ek unit mein update karo.
lessons.why: API ko abuse se bachana; concurrency ki wajah se limiter ka khud ka race sahi karna zaroori hai.
gotchas: Refill aur consume atomic ho
Clock monotonic use karo
Multi-node ke liye Redis Lua/atomic

lessons.name: Design a Thread-Safe LRU Cache
lessons.desc: LRU cache with concurrent reads/writes — naive locking kills throughput. Segmented locking is the solution.
lessons.q: Implement a thread-safe LRU cache. How do you handle concurrent reads without a write lock?
lessons.qsub: How does ConcurrentHashMap use segmented locking? What is the lock striping technique?
lessons.what: Definition: Ek global lock throughput maar deta hai. Options: segmented/striped locks, ya Caffeine jaisa library; get par bhi list reorder hoti hai isliye read-lock kaafi nahi.
lessons.why: Cache hot path hai — contention seedha latency banta hai.
gotchas: Cache stampede: ek key par sab miss → single-flight
Eviction aur get ke beech race
Memory bound zaroor rakho

lessons.name: Debugging Concurrency Bugs
lessons.desc: Race conditions and deadlocks are non-deterministic — hardest bugs to reproduce and fix.
lessons.q: How do you debug a deadlock in production? What tools and techniques do you use?
lessons.qsub: What is a thread dump? How do you analyze one to find a deadlock?
lessons.what: Definition: Approach: logs mein thread-id + timestamp, thread dump (jstack) se deadlock cycle, TSan/go test -race, stress + randomized delays, aur minimal repro.
lessons.why: Non-deterministic bugs ko tools ke bina pakadna lagbhag impossible hai.
lessons.code:
$ jstack <pid> | grep -A5 "deadlock"
$ go test -race ./...
$ clang -fsanitize=thread app.c
# stress
$ for i in $(seq 1 1000); do ./test || break; done
gotchas: Logging khud timing badal deta hai
Race detector sirf executed paths dekhta hai
Fix ke baad bhi stress run karo

lessons.name: Concurrency Models for Web Servers
lessons.desc: Thread-per-request vs thread pool vs async event-driven. Each has different performance characteristics.
lessons.q: Compare multi-threaded vs event-driven concurrency models for a web server. When does each excel?
lessons.qsub: Why does Node.js outperform Java thread-per-request for I/O-bound tasks? When does Java win?
lessons.what: Definition: Thread-per-request (Apache prefork) simple par 10k connections par fail (C10K). Pool resource bound karta hai. Event loop I/O-bound par best par CPU kaam block karta hai. Hybrid: event loop + worker pool.
lessons.why: Model workload (I/O vs CPU, connections) ke hisaab se chuno.
gotchas: Event-loop mein blocking call = sab ruk jaate
Pool size = latency ke liye critical
Little's law: concurrency = rate × latency

lessons.name: Python GIL — what it is, why it exists, when it matters
lessons.desc: The Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is a mutex in CPython that allows only one thread to execute Python bytecode at a time. It exists because CPython's reference counting is not thread-safe. It affects CPU-bound code but not I/O-bound code. Removed in Python 3.13+ (free-threaded mode, opt-in).
lessons.q: What is the Python GIL? Why does it exist and when does it matter?
lessons.qsub: How does the GIL affect CPU-bound vs I/O-bound code? What is the free-threaded mode in Python 3.13?
terms: CPython mein ek time par ek thread bytecode chalata hai.
I/O par GIL release hota hai — threads kaam karte hain.
lessons.what: Definition: GIL CPython ke reference counting ko safe rakhta hai. CPU-bound threads parallel nahi chalte; I/O (sockets, files) ya C extensions (NumPy) GIL release karte hain. Python 3.13+ mein free-threaded build experimental hai.
lessons.why: Galat model chuna to 8 threads se bhi speed nahi badhegi.
lessons.code:
import threading, time
def cpu(): sum(i*i for i in range(10**7))
t=time.time()
ts=[threading.Thread(target=cpu) for _ in range(4)]
[x.start() for x in ts]; [x.join() for x in ts]
print(time.time()-t)   # ≈ 4× single, parallel nahi
gotchas: GIL data race se nahi bachata (x += 1 race hai)
NumPy/IO GIL release karte hain
Free-threaded Python abhi default nahi

lessons.name: Threading in Python — threading module, daemon threads, Thread(target=)
lessons.desc: Python's threading module creates OS threads. Due to the GIL, threads don't help CPU-bound tasks but do help I/O-bound tasks (network, file I/O). Daemon threads die when the main thread exits. join() waits for thread completion.
lessons.q: When would you use Python threading? Why doesn't it help with CPU-bound work?
lessons.qsub: What is a daemon thread? How do you use Thread(target=func, args=()) and join()?
terms: Main exit par band, bina wait ke.
lessons.what: Definition: threading I/O-bound concurrency ke liye. Thread(target=fn, args=...), start(), join(). Daemon threads program exit nahi rokte.
lessons.why: Network/file wait overlap karna sabse aasaan: ThreadPoolExecutor.
gotchas: Thread(target=f()) — call mat karo, f pass karo
Daemon thread ka cleanup nahi hota
Exceptions thread ke andar silently mar jaate hain

lessons.name: asyncio — event loop, coroutines, await, asyncio.gather()
lessons.desc: asyncio provides single-threaded concurrency via an event loop. async/await defines coroutines. asyncio.gather() runs multiple coroutines concurrently. asyncio creates tasks that interleave during I/O waits. No GIL contention because single-threaded.
lessons.q: How does asyncio work? What is the difference between asyncio.gather() and asyncio.create_task()?
lessons.qsub: When should you use asyncio vs threading? What is the event loop and how does it schedule coroutines?
lessons.what: Definition: asyncio single thread par cooperative multitasking karta hai. await par task suspend hota hai aur loop dusra chalata hai. Blocking call (time.sleep, requests) poora loop rok deta hai.
lessons.why: Hazaaron network connections kam memory se — threads se zyada scalable.
lessons.code:
import asyncio, aiohttp
async def fetch(s, u):
    async with s.get(u) as r: return r.status
async def main():
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as s:
        print(await asyncio.gather(*[fetch(s,u) for u in urls]))
asyncio.run(main())
gotchas: time.sleep ki jagah asyncio.sleep
Blocking code ke liye asyncio.to_thread
await bhoole coroutine run hi nahi hota

lessons.name: multiprocessing — bypassing the GIL, shared memory, Process(target=)
lessons.desc: multiprocessing spawns separate processes, each with its own Python interpreter and GIL. Bypasses the GIL for CPU-bound work. Communicate via Queue, Pipe, or shared memory (Value, Array, Manager). Overhead of process creation and IPC.
lessons.q: How does multiprocessing bypass the GIL? What are the tradeoffs vs threading?
lessons.qsub: What is the difference between multiprocessing.Queue and queue.Queue? When would you use shared memory vs message passing?
lessons.what: Definition: multiprocessing alag processes chalata hai, isliye CPU-bound kaam true parallel hota hai. Data pickling se jaata hai (overhead); shared_memory se zero-copy sharing possible.
lessons.why: GIL bypass karke multi-core ka poora fayda.
lessons.code:
from multiprocessing import Pool
def square(n): return n*n
if __name__ == '__main__':      # zaroori (spawn on mac/win)
    with Pool() as p:
        print(p.map(square, range(10)))
gotchas: if __name__ == '__main__' guard bhoolna infinite spawn
Lambda/closures pickle nahi hote
Chhote tasks mein overhead benefit khata hai
